A child in New York died after contracting measles, marking the state’s first death linked to the disease in 30 years, authorities said on Monday. The child died in Lewis County in the north of New York, according to county and state health authorities. “I am heartbroken to learn that a child in Lewis County has died after contracting measles,” New York Governor Kathy Hochul said in a statement. “As a mother and grandmother, I cannot imagine what this family is going through.” Hochul, a Democrat, appeared to connect the death to Trump administration health policies, saying it was “a devastating reminder of what’s at stake when Washington deliberately erodes decades of progress in protecting Americans from preventable illnesses.” Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources The United States is facing its worst measles outbreak in 35 years. As of October 29, the Centres for Disease Control and Prevention reported 4,834 cases in 47 states. Hochul declared a disaster emergency in New York in October, following measles outbreaks in the state and neighbouring states. North Korea rejects US accusation over $6.3bn Binance hack Prosecutors seek retrial of mother accused of killing her three children US, Nigeria step up war against sextortion, romance scams Measles was declared eradicated in the US in 2000 after years of effective vaccination campaigns. But the illness has made a worrying comeback in recent years as vaccine scepticism rises alongside a growing mistrust of health authorities. Measles causes fever, respiratory symptoms, painful rashes and, in severe cases, pneumonia and brain inflammation, which can lead to death. The disease continues to claim tens of thousands of lives around the world every year. AFP Kindly share this story:
